patch_description: Structural redesign around a composable multi-stage filtering pipeline. Each filtering stage is a self-contained module implementing a common `FilterStage` interface (`apply(signal) -> filtered`), orchestrated by a `SignalPipeline` class that chains stages. This replaces the monolithic function body with: (1) reflection-padded zero-phase Savitzky-Golay stage (used three times with progressively smaller windows — the third pass directly attacks the weakest smoothness metric), (2) a slope-stabilization stage that suppresses spurious directional reversals by majority-vote over local slope signs, and (3) a trend-locking stage using local linear regression to preserve genuine trend dynamics and penalize false reversals. The zero-phase construction (row-0 of pinv(AᵀA)·Aᵀ) is retained per stage, so lag error stays controlled while noise reduction scales with stage count. The pipeline architecture improves maintainability (stages tunable independently), efficiency (precomputed convolution kernels), and allows per-stage re-measurement of the four objectives.
